7qyh1o:203: Traditional diffusion model improvements usually happen during training (collecting more data, tuning loss functions). HITS extends the improvement process to test-time, progressively enhancing quality through multiple rounds of refinement. This approach aligns with recent works on test-time compute scaling. However, HITS's layered design (boundary frames first, then full clips) is an engineering compromise—iterative refinement on full videos is extremely expensive, so processing boundary frames first concentrates the compute budget on the most critical positions.
8zie43:243: A²RD's core insight is to decouple "creative synthesis" from "consistency enforcement." Traditional end-to-end models attempt to simultaneously perform content generation and consistency maintenance in a single forward pass, leading to inconsistent training objectives — the model needs to find a balance between "generating interesting content" and "staying consistent with what came before," often optimizing neither. A²RD decomposes this contradiction into two relatively independent subproblems by introducing an agentic pipeline and Memory mechanism: the generator is responsible for "creation," while the Agent + Memory are responsible for "recall and planning." This decoupling is easier to implement in engineering because the generator and consistency modules can be optimized separately.
